newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products weak with futures, supply.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products weak with futures, supply.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were all weaker on Thursday, traders said.
Naphtha prices fell a notional $6 to $221/$223 cif, tracking a selloff in Northwest Europe where the grip on the prompt market let up slightly, at least for the moment.
Gasoline was unchanged to slightly lower to reflect crude's recent selloff and weakness in northwestern Europe, where the closed arbitrage to the States has loosened the supply picture.
But traders said the Med still looks tight, with all cargoes fixed for the month of February and demand coming from Africa for middle and low octane material.
Gas oil lost up to $5 a tonne pressured by weak premiums and sharply lower IPE gas oil futures down +$4.50 from Wednesday.
Traders said activity was very slender despite continued talk of building cargoes to take out of the region.
"People are just talking fob at the moment, local Med demand is really pretty bad," said one trader.
Russian cargoes were particularly well supplied with numbers a touch under the high cif quotes -75 cents that a cargo was done at on Wednesday.
Low sulphur fuel oil was weaker amid fresh news of more fixtures from transatlantic sources, traders said.

Offers for cargoes arriving into Italy in early March were seen at $110 cif, a fall of around $2 a tonne. Bearish data from Italian trade grouping Unione Petrolifera, showing that Italy's power sector consumed 33 percent less fuel oil in January than in the same month last year, added to the gloom.

High sulphur fuel oil was broadly steady. Med swaps were pegged at around $88 fob Med for March. High sulphur straight-run Suez cargoes were heard placed into refineries at p+c prices. Dealers assessed the Suez market at around cif high +$7, cif Med.
